import Mathlib.Algebra.DualNumber
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Operations
import AlgebraicJacobian.Tangent.NilpotentThickeningFree

/-!
# Chart triviality over the dual numbers

The **first input of the tangent/`H¹` geometric middle** of
`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` (`semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok`), in the
concrete dual-number spelling: *an invertible module over `A[ε]` whose restriction along
`ε ↦ 0` is trivial is itself trivial.*

Geometrically this is the statement that an invertible sheaf on `C ×_k Spec k[ε]` trivial
along `ε ↦ 0` is trivial on each base-changed affine chart of a 2-affine cover — which is
what turns the class into a single transition unit on the overlap and so feeds the two-chart
Čech unit-cocycle engine of `Picard/Pic0DualNumberCocycle.lean` §6. On an affine chart
`V = Spec A` the base change is `Spec A[ε]` (`DualNumber.baseChangeAlgEquiv` of that file,
combined with mathlib's `pullbackSpecIso`), so the geometric statement reduces to the
algebra proved here.

## Main results

* `DualNumber.augIdeal_mul_self_eq_bot` — the augmentation ideal `ker(A[ε] → A)` is
  **square-zero**. This is where "first-order deformation" enters, and it is the only
  property of the dual numbers the argument uses.
* `DualNumber.ker_fstHom_eq_span_eps` — that kernel is exactly `(ε)`, so a consumer holding
  either spelling can use the other.
* `DualNumber.isNilpotent_ker_fstHom` / `DualNumber.isNilpotent_span_eps` — nilpotency, the
  hypothesis of the general statement in `Picard/NilpotentThickeningFree.lean`.
* `DualNumber.free_of_cyclic_mod_eps` — the chart statement: an invertible `A[ε]`-module in
  which every element agrees with a multiple of a fixed `m` modulo `(ε)·M` is free.

## What this does and does not close

It closes the *chart-triviality* clause of the geometric middle, for arbitrary affine charts
and with no finiteness hypothesis on the sections (see the discussion in
`Picard/NilpotentThickeningFree.lean` — the nilpotent Nakayama iteration is what buys that).
The two remaining clauses of the middle are the identification
`Γ(V ×_k Spec k[ε], 𝒪) ≅ Γ(V, 𝒪)[ε]` — already available as
`DualNumber.baseChangeAlgEquiv` — and the statement that under these identifications a
kernel element goes to its transition unit, which is the genuinely cocycle-level step and
is still open.

As recorded in the docstring of `semilinearComparison_cotangentSpaceDual_h1Cok` and
confirmed from the sibling project (inbox I-0495, 2026-07-28), none of this needs Hilbert 90
or any henselian cover-splitting brick: the thickening is square-zero, which is precisely
the hypothesis discharged by `augIdeal_mul_self_eq_bot` here.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u v

open TrivSqZeroExt DualNumber

namespace DualNumber

variable (A : Type u) [CommRing A]

/-- **The augmentation ideal of the dual numbers is square-zero.** The kernel of
`A[ε] → A`, `x ↦ x.fst`, consists of the elements with vanishing constant term, and the
product of two such has both components zero: the `fst` component is a product of `fst`s,
and the `snd` component of a product is `a.fst * b.snd + b.fst * a.snd`.

This is the single property of the dual numbers that the chart-triviality argument uses —
everything else is the general nilpotent statement of
`Picard/NilpotentThickeningFree.lean`. -/
theorem augIdeal_mul_self_eq_bot :
    RingHom.ker (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom A A A) * RingHom.ker (TrivSqZeroExt.fstHom A A A) = ⊥ := by
  refine le_antisymm (Ideal.mul_le.mpr fun a ha b hb => ?_) bot_le
  have ha' : a.fst = 0 := ha
  have hb' : b.fst = 0 := hb
  refine Ideal.mem_bot.mpr (TrivSqZeroExt.ext ?_ ?_)
  · simp [TrivSqZeroExt.fst_mul, ha']
  · simp [TrivSqZeroExt.snd_mul, ha', hb']

107:theorem isNilpotent_span_eps : IsNilpotent (Ideal.span {(ε : DualNumber A)}) := by

kind: issue
body: 'THE TASK-STATUS/ROADMAP COUPLING OF I-0386 FIRED AGAIN TODAY, and this time
  it closed a node whose owner had just written down that it must not close
  Third occurrence of the hazard recorded in memory `I-0386` ("`horizon task set <id>
  --status done|cancelled` ALSO REWRITES THE ROADMAP ROWS IN THAT TASK''S `roadmap_refs`").
  Filing as an issue for a human because the memory item has not stopped it, and the
  failure is now silent corruption of another agent''s stated decision rather than
  a nuisance.
  ## What happened
  At `2026-07-28T06:04:16` task `ajc-etale-pic` was set `running` -> `done`. In the
  same instant, all four rows in its `roadmap_refs` were rewritten:
  - `AJC.jacobian.assembly` `pending` -> `done`
  - `AJC.picrep` `pending` -> `done`
  - `AJC.picrep.assembly` `pending` -> `done`
  - `AJC.picrep.rational-point` `active` -> `done`
  Three of those are defensible. `AJC.jacobian.assembly` is not, and the reason it
  is not was written down **three minutes earlier** by that same task, on team thread
  `I-0493`: *"I own AJC.jacobian.assembly (it is in my roadmap_refs) and I am NOT
  marking it done."* It then gave the measurement — $\texttt{picardJacobianWitness}$
  reports `sorryAx`, entering through five named open obligations — and said the all-children-done
  warning should be left standing deliberately.
  So the tool overrode an explicit, reasoned, contemporaneous decision by the agent
  that owned the row, with no mention of the roadmap in the command''s output.
  ## Why the existing memory is not enough
  `I-0386`''s mitigation is a discipline: read `roadmap_refs` before a terminal status,
  then re-assert each row''s status afterwards. That fails here for a structural reason
  — the task''s **last** action is setting its own terminal status, so there is no
  "afterwards" in which it can repair the damage. An agent following the memory perfectly
  still loses.
  ## Suggested fixes, in order of preference
  1. **Do not propagate.** A task''s terminal status should not write roadmap rows
  at all; the two collections mean different things (a task is a unit of work, a milestone
  is a unit of mathematics), which is exactly why the workspace keeps milestones when
  it cancels duplicate tasks.
